assumptions: HEURISTIC: random-control support occupancy is approximated by unordered multiset counts binomial(B+m-1,m).
UNTESTED: a coordinate family can retain final expansion while compressing an intermediate split support.
MODEL-BOUND: explicit Python support maps model a fixed-curve relation compiler, not an optimized cryptographic implementation.
falsification_conditions: No coordinate family retains at least 0.8x random target success while reducing advice entries or online group operations to at most 0.8x random in three instances spanning at least two q sizes.
Any signal vanishes under sign-canonical, sign-complete, shuffled-source, or matched-random controls.
Offline group operations exceed 4.0x random or independent arithmetic verification fails.
interpretation_limits: The 12-16 bit sweep cannot establish an asymptotic exponent.
A fixed-curve compiler result does not establish a single-instance generic ECDLP break.
The experiment stops before relation-matrix rank, linear algebra, and individual logarithm descent.
A promotion signal requires a later source-tagged implementation and red-team audit.
hypothesis.mechanism: A coordinate-defined factor base may have nearly random m-fold support but smaller two-, three-, or four-fold split supports. A fixed-curve compiler can store those split supports and query arbitrary targets by enumerating the smaller side and looking up exact complements.
hypothesis.statement: At least one tested coordinate factor base retains near-random m-fold target coverage while reducing split-compiler advice or online query work under matched cardinality and symmetry controls.
